subject: chemistry
title: Chromatography and Magnetism
welcome_lead: Split rainbow inks with paper, or pluck iron out of a pile with a magnet.
meta_desc: Use chromatography and magnetism to separate mixtures in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now choose the right separation method for any mixture.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Chromatography separates the different coloured dyes in inks. Dot the ink on paper, dip the bottom in solvent (often water), and watch the colours spread up the paper at different speeds.

Each dye forms its own spot. A pure dye gives just one spot.

A simple way to remove iron from a mixture is to use a magnet. Iron, cobalt and nickel are magnetic; most other materials are not.

Iron filings out of sand.

Ask: are the parts solid or liquid? Can they dissolve? Are any magnetic?

Filtration for insoluble solids, evaporation for soluble solids, distillation for liquids, chromatography for dyes, and magnets for iron.
